rules: A label names a library skill that a careful engineer would want the agent of the item to have, in full or as an open-when item, for the work that the item's own text names. Lookup is the one that should find it by the skill's declared claims: A for a facts claim (writes_code, languages, role), B for an activity, touches, quality or artefact claim, C when no claim fits the item's form and only a free-text need can find it.

rex-code-essentials is the one label for the coding rules of a code task. The four rulebooks (rex-code-philosophy, rex-code-commenting, rex-code-ergonomics, rex-code-error-writing) are its open-when items (spec D18), so they are not labelled again as separate needs. They are labelled only where the item's work is the rulebooks themselves (0h0d1109wo-T1 and its reviewer).

rex-code-tests-integration-testing is labelled only when a test crosses to a real outside program, service or database (its header: the real outside world), not for a test that runs this repo's own binary on a fixture folder in tests/integration/.

rex-code-failure-policy is labelled when the item's text names what code does with bad outside input or adds an error code or variant: a finding and never a panic, not_found, a bad cursor, input that must not stop the run.
rex-code-folder-management is labelled when the item creates a new module or folder of code with its mod line, or must split a file at the 500-line limit.

A reviewer writes no code. Its review method is rex-pr-review, a listed skill outside plugin/library, so a reviewer is none in library unless its text names a library skill's check or reviews skill text.
An item's own output is never its label: rex-code-essentials is not a label of 0h0d1109wo-T1, which writes it.

needs_rules: Step 3, after the forms were read and before any search was run on them. Each free-text need of runs 1 and 2 lists every skill that serves it, library or pool, or none. The run field names the form it came from; score-hits.ts ignores it, so per-run label files are made from this one with a jq filter on run.

A pool skill is named only when its folder name is the very technology that the need names (sqlite, claude-code, mcp-server-builder, tdd). Its text was not read: the gate A README lets only the scripts read the pool. Each such label carries basis.
rex-code-essentials and rex-skill-language are not labelled for a need that is the item's own output, except that rex-skill-language counts for the style of text that the item writes into it.
